resources.string: An iconic wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars. It is one of the most recognizable structures in the world.
The world\'s largest art museum and a historic monument in Paris. Home to masterpieces like the Mona Lisa and the Venus de Milo.
A medieval Catholic cathedral on the Île de la Cité. It is a masterpiece of French Gothic architecture.
Stands at the center of the Place Charles de Gaulle. It honors those who fought and died for France in the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars.
Housed in a former railway station, this museum holds mainly French art dating from 1848 to 1914, including the largest collection of Impressionist and post-Impressionist masterpieces in the world.

A complex building in the Beaubourg area, it houses the Public Information Library, the Musée National d\'Art Moderne, and IRCAM, a centre for music and acoustic research. Known for its high-tech architecture.

A museum that was opened in 1919, dedicated to the works of the French sculptor Auguste Rodin. It has two sites: the Hôtel Biron and surrounding grounds in central Paris, and just outside Paris at Rodin\'s old home.
Famous for its simple menu: a green salad with walnuts, followed by steak frites with their signature sauce. Expect a queue!
A historic "bouillon" restaurant offering traditional French cuisine at very affordable prices in a stunning Belle Époque dining room.
Located in the Marais district, this spot is legendary for serving one of the best falafel sandwiches in the world. A must-try for street food lovers.
A world-renowned pastry chef, his boutiques offer exquisite macarons, chocolates, and pastries that are as beautiful as they are delicious.
